22559994.reason: Four well-resolved detached eclipse profiles comprise two deep same-kind events in S64/S100 and two shallower same-kind events in S37/S101. The two kinds each recur; their alternating depth is not counted as additional same-kind recurrence. The deep profiles lose about 17-22% and the shallow profiles about 8% of local SAP flux. Sector-dependent dilution explains some depth differences but is not fitted here.
22559994.timing: The deep span is 1036.694969 d over an adopted 22 cycles; the shallow span 1790.654283 d over 38 cycles independently agrees to 0.00066 d. Neighboring integer counts for the deep pair fail the shallow span. Timing alone also permits a 94.244997 d family and shorter rational families; the bounded shorter-alias null tests reject P/2 through P/6. The 47.12 d assignment is favored by Gaia but is not a unique timing-only orbital solution.
22559994.limits: Repeated target-region eclipses are secure. Gaia orbital association has persistent 2.2-2.8 local linear-sigma offsets, and a 94.245 d timing family remains. Close unresolved companions and changing dilution remain possible.
22559994.next: Obtain a new resolved same-kind eclipse and radial velocities; test the 47/94 d orbital alternatives and Gaia epoch geometry.

65684549.reason: A train of compact resolved dips repeats throughout S59, S73 and S86, separated by approximately 1.137 d. Individual depths change with sector and baseline quality. These are discrete contact-shaped deficits rather than a smooth tidal wave.
65684549.timing: The 1.13719 d recurrence is measured from ten representative dips spanning three sectors. Within-sector cadence and dozens of repeated events anchor this clock; the 0.008 d timing RMS is larger than formal fit errors. This is an eclipse recurrence, and a twice-longer orbital period with similar opposite eclipses is not excluded. The train cannot be the selected 20.825 d Gaia orbit: many cycles occur inside a single Gaia period.
65684549.limits: The 6.46 arcsec G=9.82 neighbor is 7.33 times the target G-band flux and easily capable of supplying the eclipse loss. TESS alone may not resolve which member is eclipsing. Gaia association fails. The separately extracted 3x3 aperture dilutes the train strongly in the bright blended PSF; small repeated deficits remain but do not discriminate ownership.
65684549.next: Resolve target and 6.46 arcsec neighbor during one short-clock eclipse; determine which star owns the train and search that source's known-variable identity.

70554665.next: Obtain a further eclipse with independent observing equipment and refine the ephemeris.

122766753.reason: Many compact resolved dips recur in S19, S59, S73 and S86. Sparse S19 sampling alone would be weak, but the dense later sectors establish repeated narrow morphology. The train's event spacing is about 2.2093 d. The selected target is not retained as the eclipsing source: four event-local difference images locate the positive deficit on the 19.74 arcsec neighbor rather than the target.
122766753.timing: Nine representative events fit a 2.20928 d recurrence with 0.0034 d residual RMS. Several consecutive same-looking events within one sector constrain the short clock. A twice-longer orbital period with nearly similar opposite eclipses remains possible. Neither recurrence is the selected 27.6256 d Gaia orbit; isolated conjunction coincidences are not orbital association.
122766753.limits: REFUTED_SOURCE for the selected Gaia/TIC target. Four separate S59 event-local differences all peak at pixel (4,5); their centroids are approximately 0.04-0.20 pixel from Gaia DR3 201206302856438528 and about one pixel from the target. This repeated local PSF displacement is stronger evidence than an unresolved-blend possibility. The phase-stack image is structured and gives a conflicting centroid; because stacking spans variable backgrounds and broad baseline states, it is not accepted as a reliable localization and does not override four consistent clean local event differences. A calibrated PRF fit or second orientation could test this adjudication, but target attribution is refuted within the bounded representative evidence. The neighbor remains a separate characterization lead, with no independent source/novelty review or claim substituted into this queue.
122766753.next: Perform a separate identity, catalogue and PRF/resolved-photometry review of neighbor Gaia DR3 201206302856438528; establish its true orbital period without silently relabeling the selected target.
